analysis.investment_thesis: Can Fin Homes is a financial company — mortgage finance — and the Magic Formula explicitly excludes this category because debt is the raw material of the business, not a capital structure choice, making EBIT/EV and ROIC meaningless. I cannot score it on my framework, and I won't pretend otherwise.
key_strengths: Low P/E of 11.87x and Forward P/E of 10.49x — cheap on reported earnings by conventional metrics
Strong net profit CAGR of 22.1% over 3 years (INR 471 Cr FY22 → INR 857 Cr FY25), indicating healthy loan book growth
Canara Bank parentage and affordable housing focus provide franchise stability and a reliable liability franchise
key_risks: D/E of 6.59x — leverage is the business model, but it amplifies any credit cycle or liquidity shock nonlinearly
Finance costs growing at 29.3% CAGR vs. revenue at 18.8% CAGR — NIM compression risk if rates stay elevated
Magic Formula exclusion: I have no reliable way to assess capital efficiency or earnings quality using my standard framework
red_flags: Operating CF was negative in FY22 (–INR 3,916 Cr) and FY23 (–INR 4,044 Cr) — characteristic of HFC capital deployment, but not reassuring
Total debt of INR 34,898 Cr against equity of INR 5,067 Cr means any asset quality deterioration is amplified significantly
Framework exclusion is itself a red flag for this style of investing — I don't invest where I can't compute the formula
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Can Fin Homes is an Indian housing finance company — the Magic Formula I created in 'The Little Book That Beats the Market' explicitly excludes financial firms and utilities because the capital structure of these businesses is fundamentally different from operating companies. A bank or HFC's liabilities ARE its inputs; computing EBIT/EV or ROIC for such a business produces nonsense numbers. So I won't force the formula onto an incompatible business.

For what it's worth, Can Fin Homes looks modestly priced by conventional HFC metrics — P/E under 12x, solid ROE near 17%, and Canara Bank's institutional backing. But operating CF was sharply negative in FY22-23, finance costs are growing faster than revenues, and D/E of 6.6x means thin cushion for error. If you're a value investor using different tools (like P/B vs. ROE for financials), this merits a deeper look — but it's outside my circle of competence as defined by my formula.
